The laws assign distinct roles to washing, elapsed time, priestly observation, sacrifice, and declaration.
Commands, declarations, substances, speech, divine promises, and Christ’s action receive different grammatical roles across the sources.
The procedures repeatedly distinguish washing from the later end of uncleanness.
Later sources reuse washing and cleansing language while changing the object, agent, literary form, and claimed outcome.
The corpus preserves nonmoral bodily statuses and also uses defilement language for violent or harmful conduct.
